title: Profile ingestion, runner-compatibility matrix and sampled-prompt allocator
creator: Asha Patel
description: Improve the benchmark harness pipeline to produce deterministic, publishable performance profiles during model onboarding. Introduces a runner-compatibility matrix, idempotent ingestion for profile artifacts, and a sampled-prompt allocator that balances coverage and cost across eval runners. This work reduces flaky profile publishes, speeds onboarding, and makes version pinning for serving more reliable.
background: Model onboarding currently produces profiles with non-uniform runner coverage and occasional publish failures caused by runner incompatibilities or dataset/format drift. Profiles are used by runtime and Console rollout logic, so instability here causes served models to be mis-pinned or fallback incorrectly. We need a standardized compatibility matrix that declares which runners and runner-configs are compatible with a given dataset/prompt set and an allocator that deterministically maps sampled prompts to runners to preserve reproducibility across runs.
scope: Add a runner-compatibility metadata artifact, make profile ingestion idempotent and timestamped, implement sampled-prompt allocator with seeds, extend harness to emit compatibility diagnostics, and wire publishing flow to validate compatibility before publishing. Update Console profile display to show runner coverage and ingestion status.
out_of_scope: Major dataset schema redesign, retraining or annotator work, and runtime serving changes beyond pin lookup behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Harness emits a runner-compatibility artifact (CSV or JSON) alongside each profile run
Profile ingestion endpoint accepts idempotent publish token and rejects duplicate publishes
Sampled-prompt allocator produces identical prompt-to-runner mapping given same seed and profile input
Publishing flow validates compatibility; incompatible runner mappings fail publish with actionable error messages
Console shows per-profile runner coverage, ingestion timestamp, and compatibility warnings
End-to-end test demonstrates reproducible profile generation across two runs on CI with identical seeds
design_notes: Compatibility matrix format: rows are runner-types (e.g., cpu, gpu-v100, gpus-ampere-q8), columns are dataset features (max_seq, token_type, structured_output). Values: supported|partial|unsupported
Idempotency: publish request must include profile-hash and publish-token. Ingestion service will respond 200 with existing resource URL if hash + token seen within 30 days

Sampling: allocator uses stratified sampling by scenario tag and difficulty bucket; mapping is a deterministic RNG seeded with (profile-hash, run-timestamp-truncated-to-minute) or explicit seed passed in CI
Diagnostics: harness emits runner-compatibility-check.log with mismatches and suggested remediation (e.g., prompt truncation or quantization profile change)
Rollback: publish uses staging state. Only after compatibility validation and a checksum verification do we promote profile to stable catalog
implementation_tasks: Add compatibility matrix generator to harness runner shim (ENG change)
Implement idempotent publish API in profile service and update schema to persist publish_token and profile_hash
Build sampled-prompt allocator library (stratified + seedable RNG) and integrate into harness sampling phase
Emit compatibility diagnostics and add automated remediation hints
Update profile publishing workflow to validate compatibility and stage/promotion steps
Add Console UI panels for runner coverage and ingestion metadata
Create CI e2e that runs harness twice with same seed and asserts identical profile artifact hashes
progress_updates: 2026-03-06: Spike completed for compatibility matrix format; agreed on CSV-first with JSON fallback for complex fields
2026-03-08: Prototype sampled-prompt allocator implemented in Python harness branch; deterministic mapping validated locally
2026-03-10: API design for idempotent publish reviewed with backend; minor change to token TTL requested
2026-03-12: First end-to-end run on staging produced a compatibility mismatch; diagnostics suggested trimming structured-output fields as fix
decisions: Use CSV as primary interchange for human readability and backward compatibility with existing tooling
Keep compatibility matrix versioned alongside profile (compat_v1) to allow future schema evolution
Deterministic seed must be explicitly set by CI or devs; default harness seed will be time-based but must be logged in artifacts
risks: Large datasets may increase allocator memory footprint; mitigation: reservoir sampling and on-disk iterators
False negatives in compatibility checks could block valid profiles; mitigation: add lenient mode with warnings for non-critical mismatches
Coordination overhead with Console and profile-service teams for schema changes
test_plan: Unit tests for allocator deterministic behavior across seed changes
Compatibility matrix unit tests with synthetic runner/dataset feature combos
Integration test: harness -> profile-service publish with idempotency token; repeated publish should be a no-op
E2E CI: two harness runs with same seed produce identical profile hashes; Console shows ingestion metadata
Chaos test: simulate runner versions missing; ensure publish fails with clear remediation message
metrics: Time-to-publish median (target < 3 minutes for typical profiles)
Percent of profiles with full runner coverage vs partial
Number of reproducible profile hash matches between repeated runs
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged release: default off for production onboarding; enabled for staging and canary orgs
Pilot with two ongoing onboarding efforts (internal B2B testbeds) for one week
Collect metrics and iterate on compatibility heuristics before wide release
Coordinate with Console team for a synchronized feature flag flip to display new metadata
notes: We should coordinate with Applied ML when compatibility suggests quantization profile changes
Consider adding a small human-in-the-loop step for first few publishes to avoid noisy false-positives
